notes: Clicked for credits for turns on end, banking 30 credits with nothing installed, while the Corp scored three agendas from thinly protected remotes it never contested; it won mostly off Archives steals and a final facetank of Anansi.

Kept installing an agenda and advancing it once each turn behind a single Tsarevna the Runner was happy to facetank, so four agendas were stolen there in a row; it never added ice, never scored and never punished the tags.

Sat at 0 credits for about 15 turns, running HQ four times a turn into Virtual Service Agent only to see Bellona and Degree Mill it could not afford to steal; it never clicked for credits and only won because the Corp decked.
Solid Weyland play that scored three Send a Message from iced remotes, though it was slow and floated 40+ credits; losing the turn 1 agenda to Inside Job was mostly bad luck.
Tight, aggressive play: it set up installs so it could pay Degree Mill's additional cost, stole it twice and closed with a Trick Shot double access.
Clicked for credits and discarded almost every turn without building a remote, leaving HQ behind one Ping where four agendas were stolen; the Oppo Research into End of the Line was its only threat.
Ran an empty Archives for about eight turns while the Corp sat on a full HQ, then three times pumped Audrey and pitched cards into Semak-samun without breaking it; it got there eventually through HQ.
Clicked for credits for five straight turns up to 26 with nothing installed, then after seeing Anansi deal 4 net damage it ran back into it with a near-empty grip and flatlined.
Never installed an agenda; for about 15 turns it clicked for credits and discarded with 20+ credits while HQ sat behind one Ping, and it never cashed in the Runner's many tags.
A clean Weyland game that scored three agendas from a well-iced remote with good economy; minor oddities include parking Spin Doctor in the scoring remote.
Left R&D unprotected all game and lost Fujii there, but scored from its remote and set up a neat kill with Oppo Research, the False Lead click drain and End of the Line.
Left tags up against an Oppo/End of the Line deck and ate an EotL, then spent the middle game on repeated Archives runs while the Corp scored; it rebuilt late and won through HQ and R&D.
Left R&D without ice for 11 turns while the Runner stole four agendas from it, clicked for credits and discarded most turns, and fired three Oppo Research with no follow-up.

Stuck at 0 credits for about 20 turns, running R&D four times a turn to re-see the same top card and never clicking for credits; it let the Corp score Degree Mill and Bellona behind a lone Ping and won only by decking.
Good early HQ pressure with Sable and Boomerang, but it lost tempo on Archives runs and money clicks and could not contest the remote while the Corp scored twice; the R&D steal closed it out.
Spent the first two turns clicking for credits with no ice anywhere while holding agendas, and lost on turn 3 to free HQ and R&D runs.
Built a decent board but spent many turns on Archives runs off its Sable mark while the Corp scored a second Send a Message uncontested; with Aumakua online it finished cleanly.
Clicked for credits and discarded for several early turns while rich, but then scored three agendas from iced remotes, landed Snare, and won when the Runner stole Sting at low grip.
Sensible net-damage plan that scored behind Semak-samun, ground the Runner down with Bladderwort and Phoneutria and flatlined it; economy was very thin for a few turns and R&D was open early.

Played the whole game on 0 credits, running R&D four times a turn to re-access the same card while naked remotes went unchecked, one of which held a Stoke the Embers the Corp scored; it won anyway off open R&D and a naked remote.
